key_insight: Energy-Based Generative Replay (EB-Gen) reduces catastrophic forgetting by using Hopfield network dynamics to generate rehearsal samples internally.
engineering_relevance: The approach could support edge-friendly continual learning, though the abstract reports image-classification benchmarks rather than solid-mechanics applications.
method: Train a Hopfield network using Equilibrium Propagation.
Generate past-task pseudo-data by relaxing a frozen copy of the network.
Rehearse generated samples while learning new classes, without an external data buffer or separate generator architecture.
evidence_signal: Class-incremental evaluations report average accuracies of 75% on Split MNIST and 64% on Split CIFAR10, with comparisons against FineTune, ER, Gen-Replay, SRC and Joint training.
watch_item: Maintaining a frozen network copy and generating replay samples still incur memory and computation costs; edge-hardware efficiency is not quantified in the abstract.
paper_title: Generative Replay for Equilibrium Propagation: Toward Edge-Friendly Continual Learning in Hopfield Networks
